# Tacet

> Environmental Risk & Comfort Twin for luxury hospitality. Predicts how external events (noise, construction, crowds, weather) will physically hit a property, then turns that into yield rules for an RMS and operational alerts for a PMS. Headless, exposed through a native MCP server. Python 3.12 / FastAPI, MIT.

Status: Built — the code runs end-to-end on the target environment. Paused / maintenance mode, no active development since July 2026. Status vocabulary: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Hospitality-Multi-agent-Architecture/blob/main/llms.txt

Tacet is the environmental-risk node of the Hospitality Multi-agent Architecture. The F&B execution node (Aetherix) is a private repo; the architecture is documented in the meta-repo.

## How it works

- Sense — public signals: Paris permits API, events, weather.
- Reason — acoustic ray-tracing over urban building polygons (OSMnx, Shapely): when a building blocks the source, a shielding penalty applies, which cuts false positives. Plus a dual-memory store (per-property idiosyncratic + cross-network aggregate).
- Expose — an MCP server returning yield rules with a mathematical Chain of Thought, so a consuming agent can explain the calculation rather than assert it.

Human-in-the-loop by design: Tacet formulates a price-modifier rule and pushes it for human approval. It never changes a price autonomously.

## Stack

Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.115, Anthropic MCP SDK, SQLAlchemy 2.0 + SQLite (dual-memory store), OSMnx, Shapely, GeoPandas. Mews and Apaleo connectors, RMS webhooks. CI on GitHub Actions.
